title: Agreement with the affine-line route on affine space
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $d\geq0$, let $p_d:X=\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space], and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the specified pro-etale twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The affine comparison at every coefficient level is specified as follows. For an affine-line projection $p:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ with standard compactification $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$, $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, define $I_S:Rp_!A(1)[2]\to A_S$ by $Rq_*j_!A(1)[2]\to Rq_*A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{t_q}A_S$. Here $t_q$ is the ordinary etale projective-line trace [def-amb-p1-trace], formed with $\mu_{\ell^r}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$ for any $r\geq1$ such that $\ell^rA=0$, and realized on the specified pro-etale Tate twist by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Define $\Gamma_{p,K}$ as the exceptional transpose of
$$
Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes_A^LRp_!A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes I_S}K,
$$
using the projection map [def-exchange-projection]. These maps are independent of $r$. Put $\Gamma_{p_0,K}=1_K$ and define $\Gamma_{p_d,K}$ as the ordered composite of these $d$ affine-line maps, with the exceptional-composition and twist-additivity isomorphisms as in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. On the domain $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum], these are exactly the named maps [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison, thm-pur-affine-line-purity, cor-pur-affine-space-purity]; the displayed construction specifies their extension to all $n\geq1$.

Specify the diagonal/DNC normalization in the smooth purity map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] as follows, as in the model paragraph of the unit. Put $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$, and let $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_d}$ be [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Let $N=N_{\Delta/W}$ and let $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,0_N)$ be the normalized comparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], with section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant]. On the normal bundle use the inverse of the integration-transposed comparison of [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], with integration [def-amb-vector-integration], transported by [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Pulling it back along $0_N$ and restricting the twist gives $\beta:C(\pi_N,0_N)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$. The dualizing orientation used in the middle arrow of the smooth purity map is $\vartheta_p=\beta\delta\alpha^{-1}:\omega_p\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$; that middle arrow uses $\vartheta_p^{-1}$.

Then this smooth purity map equals $\Gamma_{p_d,K}$ as a morphism
$$
Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rp_d^!K.
$$
For $d=0$ both maps are $1_K$.

proof.text:
Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$; it exists since $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme. The roots-of-unity sheaf is locally free of rank one over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], so its derived tensor with $A$ is its ordinary tensor. To use the coefficient identification of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] on any such scheme $T$, take the empty effective Cartier divisor: its ideal is generated by the nonzerodivisor $1$. Its projection-induced identification realizes this ordinary etale Tate line as the specified pro-etale Tate line. For any scheme pullback, first commute it with $\nu^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], then apply the roots-of-unity pullback identification of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Apply [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] at finite coefficients to the Tate line and an arbitrary ambient complex. Its tensor, unit and composition compatibilities, followed by the tensor-power associators and shift additivity, give $Lf^*(M(a)[b])\cong(Lf^*M)(a)[b]$ for the nonnegative twists used here. These fix the coherent twist restrictions and reassociations used below. The unit and the Kummer class $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ are the two summands defining $b_q$ in [def-amb-p1-trace]. For the coefficient realization of $h$, apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] to the infinity divisor on $\mathbf P^1_S$. In its affine chart that divisor is cut out by the polynomial coordinate, a nonzerodivisor over every base ring; its line bundle is $\mathcal O(1)$, as its two standard local generators show. The lemma makes this realized Kummer class independent of $r$. Full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] reflects that equality to the ordinary etale derived category after the specified coefficient identifications. The unit also is independent of $r$. Thus $b_q$, $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$, and its affine restriction $I_S$ are independent of $r$. Applying the projection formula, exceptional transpose, and ordered composition preserves that equality, so the displayed $\Gamma$ is well defined at every $n\geq1$. On the domain of the original affine-line datum its formulas are exactly those of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. For the coefficient input $K$, choose $K^{\mathrm{et}}\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $\nu_Y^*K^{\mathrm{et}}\cong K$ using [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] gives this witness the same finite Tor interval as $K$. Thus the map comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] applies to these inputs: it identifies the actual tensor projection maps, the integrations, and their exceptional transposes under the specified Tate and compact-support comparisons. In particular the ordinary integration-transposed vector-bundle isomorphism gives the pro-etale transpose of the specified pro-etale projection/integration composite. This comparison also applies at the tensor unit. Every finite-type $k$-scheme used below is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is a Noetherian ring.

Let $X=\mathbf A^d_Y$, $p=p_d$, $W=X\times_YX$, with coordinates $(x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_d)$, and let $p_1,p_2,\Delta$ be the projections and diagonal. The projection $p$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] the specified base-change arrow gives $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], the diagonal is a closed section with normal bundle $T_{X/Y}$. Explicitly its ideal is $(y_i-x_i)_{1\leq i\leq d}$; modulo its square these generators form a basis, so the normal bundle is the trivial rank-$d$ bundle over $X$. The $X$-isomorphism $h:W\to\mathbf A^d_X$, $(x,y)\mapsto(x,u=y-x)$, has inverse $(x,u)\mapsto(x,y=x+u)$ and takes $\Delta$ to the zero section. The induced map on the displayed normal bases is the identity. All schemes here are separated and finite type. The affine spaces and W restrict over affine base charts to spectra of polynomial rings; the trace compactifications are the proper finite-type projective lines of [def-amb-p1-trace]. Thus the section invariant and DNC constructions have their required domains. These coordinate statements also hold for $d=0$. For the relative hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], each chosen projective compactification is finite type over $k$ and has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; on nonempty compactifications take an integer upper bound for that dimension. Empty schemes are handled by the unique zero-object maps. This verifies the dimension hypothesis as well as the bounded-below etale-origin hypothesis whenever those hom bijections are used.

proof.text: We first prove that translating affine coordinates preserves the specified trace. For $S$ empty the assertion is the unique equality on the empty scheme. Otherwise let $S$ be separated finite type and write $t_{q}:Rq_!A(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S$ for the affine-space trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. On the parameter scheme $P=\mathbf A^d_S$, consider the universal translation $\tau(a,z)=(a,z-a)$ of $\mathbf A^d_P/P$. Since $q\tau=q$, the coherent composition comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], with the identification of the constant Tate coefficient under the isomorphism $\tau$, give an automorphism $T_\tau$ of $Rq_!A(d)[2d]$. Conjugating by $t_q$ gives an automorphism of $A_P$. Apply the fully faithful bounded-below comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] to regard this as a pro-etale automorphism; this derived endomorphism of the degree-zero sheaf $A_P$ is a unique sheaf endomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], and it is multiplication by a locally constant unit $v$ by [lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut]. At the zero parameter translation is the identity. The construction of $T_\tau$ commutes with base change of the parameter scheme: by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], restricted to these bounded-below inputs, the compact-support exchange is compatible with identities, composite changes of base and the composition comparisons, and the Tate identifications are compatible with pullback. Base-change compatibility of $t_q$ therefore gives $v|_{0(S)}=1$. Iterating clause (1) of [lem-pur-a1-components] shows that every connected component of $P$ is the inverse image of a component of $S$ and meets $0(S)$: in rank one, the inverse image of a component contains its zero-section image, and iteration gives the assertion in rank $d$. Thus $v=1$, so $t_qT_\tau=t_q$. For $d=0$ it is the identity. Specializing the parameter proves translation invariance for every section. The specific integration comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies the trace maps and their transposes on the two sites. Applying comparison pullback to the trace equality and using these identifications gives the corresponding equality on the finite etale-origin objects here; the relative Hom bijections are those of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. In particular the affine/vector-bundle comparison obtained by transposing integration is unchanged by $h$ of Step 1. This is the translation argument required in the unit's model paragraph, rather than an inference from equality on individual geometric fibers.

source.place: Proof, Agreement on the model, translation invariance and connected components

proof.text:
Denote by $P_{q,K}:Lq^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq^!K$ the transpose of integration for a rank-$d$ trivial bundle $q$, using [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity, def-amb-vector-integration] and the actual hom bijections [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. The equality of this transported transpose with the specified pro-etale projection/integration transpose is [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], on the witnesses fixed in Step 1. Set $L=A_X(d)[2d]$, $P=P_{p,A_Y}:L\to\omega_p$, $L'=A_W(d)[2d]$, and $J=P_{p_1,A_X}:L'\to\omega_{p_1}$. We prove the required base-change identity for these particular maps, without identifying two unspecified canonical orientations. Write $C_M:Lp^*Rp_!M\to Rp_{1!}Lp_2^*M$ for compact-support exchange in the diagonal square. By [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] it is precisely the transported ordinary etale exchange. The trace identity in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with base change $p:X\to Y$, is therefore $t_{p_1}C_L=Lp^*t_p$, using Step 1's Tate pullback identifications and [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Let $B:Lp_2^*\omega_p\to\omega_{p_1}$ be the specified dualizing base-change map of [def-pur-co-smoothness](3). Its transpose is $Lp^*\varepsilon_p\circ C_{\omega_p}^{-1}$. Naturality of $C$ with respect to $P$ shows that the transpose of $B\circ Lp_2^*P$ is
$$Lp^*\varepsilon_p\circ C_{\omega_p}^{-1}\circ Rp_{1!}(Lp_2^*P)
=Lp^*(\varepsilon_p\circ Rp_!P)\circ C_L^{-1}
=Lp^*t_p\circ C_L^{-1}=t_{p_1}.$$
The middle equality is the defining adjunction equation for $P$. The defining transpose of $J$ is also $t_{p_1}$, so injectivity of the same hom bijection gives $J=B\circ Lp_2^*P$. In [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\alpha=(L\Delta^*B)^{-1}$ after $p_2\Delta=1_X$. Consequently
$$\alpha\circ L\Delta^*J=P.$$
The ordinary restriction $L\Delta^*L'=L$ is Step 1's coherent Tate restriction, not exceptional pullback. Finally Step 2 identifies $J$ in coordinates $u=y-x$ with the same integration-transposed comparison in the standard-bundle coordinates. This uses equality of traces and transposes, not an unrecorded construction from the proof of the vector-bundle corollary.

source.place: Proof, Agreement on the model, base-change identification under the vector-bundle comparisons

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to $(p_1,\Delta)$, obtaining $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,0_N)$. In the global coordinates $u_i=y_i-x_i$ this is a standard affine pair. Its deformation is given by $u_i=t v_i$ and has constant family object by the standard-pair clause of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry]. The normalization clause of the DNC theorem makes $\delta$ the identity between these two standard section invariants. Write $\beta=L0_N^*(P_{\pi_N,A_X}^{-1})$, followed by Step 1's ordinary Tate restriction, so $\beta:C(\pi_N,0_N)\to A_X(d)[2d]$. The induced normal coordinates $v_i$ use the same ordered basis as $u_i$, by Step 1. With Step 2's translation invariance, the standard-pair identity says precisely $\beta\delta=(L\Delta^*J)^{-1}$. The explicitly specified diagonal/DNC normalization in the statement and in the middle arrow of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is $\theta_p=\beta\delta\alpha^{-1}$. By Step 3,
$$\theta_p=(L\Delta^*J)^{-1}\alpha^{-1}=P_{p,A_Y}^{-1}.$$
This checks the actual normalized arrows; it does not deduce equality merely from existence of isomorphisms to a twist. In rank zero the displayed coordinate lists are empty, the deformation is the constant rank-zero pair, and the same equations are identities.

source.place: Proof, standard-pair identity; unit Agreement on the model, final three sentences

proof.text:
We now prove equality for arbitrary $K$, using transposes rather than naturality alone. Put $L=A_X(d)[2d]$ and $P=P_{p,A_Y}:L\to\omega_p$. By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and Step 4, smooth purity is $\theta_{p,K}(1\otimes P)$ after twist reassociation, where $\theta_{p,K}$ is the canonical tensor arrow of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. By the explicit definition in [def-pur-co-smoothness], its exceptional transpose is the projection-formula composite with $Rp_!\omega_p\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{p,A_Y}}A_Y$. Naturality of the projection map [def-exchange-projection] with respect to $P$ moves $Rp_!P$ to this counit. Since $P$ is by definition the transpose of $t_p$, the adjunction identity gives $\varepsilon_{p,A_Y}\circ Rp_!P=t_p$. The resulting transpose is therefore exactly
$$Rp_!(Lp^*K\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes Rp_!L\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes t_p}K.$$
This is the defining transpose of the ordinary comparison in [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], and [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies it with the specified pro-etale defining transpose of $P_{p,K}$. The projection maps used here are invertible by the unconditional finite-level statement [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. Its field and coefficient hypotheses are exactly those fixed here, and $p$ is separated of finite type. For its base coefficient use the bounded constructible etale witness $K^{\mathrm{et}}$ from Step 1, with its finite Tor interval reflected by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii). Its source coefficient $L=A_X(d)[2d]$ is the realization of the ordinary shifted Tate line, hence bounded constructible. For the component with $\omega_p$, Step 4 gives the witness $P:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$, so the same lemma applies without any Tor assumption on a general source coefficient. The lemma identifies its actual pro-etale transformation with [def-exchange-projection], so its naturality in the source coefficient gives precisely the square used above. This uses no six-functor datum. Equality of transposes under the actual adjunction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] proves that smooth purity equals $P_{p,K}$.

source.place: Proof, final assertion that the two assemblies agree, with the coefficient argument expanded

proof.text:
We establish the projection compatibility needed for this ordered tower, rather than assuming it from a six-functor datum. Write $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and $\pi_u$ for the counit-defined proper projection map of [def-exchange-projection]. For composable proper $u,v$, identify $R_{vu}$ with $R_vR_u$ by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. The two maps
$$\pi_{vu;M,N},\qquad R_v(\pi_{u;M,P_vN})\circ\pi_{v;R_uM,N}$$
are equal under the pullback/tensor identifications. Indeed [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives the composite counit $\varepsilon_u\circ P_u\varepsilon_vR_u$. Transpose the two maps under $P_uP_v\dashv R_vR_u$: both first distribute $P_uP_v$ over $(R_vR_uM)\otimes N$, apply $P_u\varepsilon_{v,R_uM}$ to its first factor and then $\varepsilon_{u,M}$ to that factor, leaving $P_uP_vN$ unchanged. Naturality and the composition compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify the intervening tensor comparisons. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves equality. For an identity map the same calculation is the triangle identity. Iterating the same counit composite gives the equality for all parenthesizations. The same transpose check with two base factors $N_1,N_2$ proves the tensor-action identity: the one-step projection for $N_1\otimes N_2$ equals the successive projections for $N_1$ and $N_2$, with tensor and pullback associators inserted. Both transposes distribute pullback over three tensor factors and apply the single counit to the $R_uM$ factor; associativity and unit compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] make them identical. The open-extension version preserves the same three pure tensor factors, so has the same identity. This also proves the tensor-action identity for the compactification composite. Thus extracting the coefficient $K$ before or after the Tate-line factors gives exactly the same map. These are identities of maps before imposing any invertibility or Tor condition.

For the proper/open interchange use [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], evaluated at a finite constant coefficient level. In its notation write $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$ for the proper maps, $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ for the opens; the commutative square is $pk=ir$. Its normalized interchange $\gamma:i_!R_r\to R_pk_!$ is the mate of $\alpha:P_pi_!\to k_!P_r$, where $\alpha$ is open base change followed by the specified clopen projection. Denote by $\delta_j$ the open tensor map of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. For $M$ on $V$ and $N$ on $T$, the tensor identity to check is
$$\gamma_{M\otimes P_rP_iN}\,i_!(\pi_{r;M,P_iN})\,\delta_i
=R_p(\delta_k)\,\pi_{p;k_!M,N}\,(\gamma_M\otimes1).$$
Both sides go from $i_!R_rM\otimes N$ to $R_pk_!(M\otimes P_rP_iN)$. Transpose under $P_p\dashv R_p$ and substitute the stated mate formula for $\gamma$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_p$ and its triangle identity reduce both sides to the map which uses $\alpha_{R_rM}$ on the first factor and finally applies $k_!(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1)$. The only tensor comparison in this reduction is that $\alpha$ commutes with tensor: for its open-base-change part both routes preserve the section and its local pure tensor; for the clopen projection both are the identity on the chosen component and zero on its complement. The open tensor identification is the sheaf map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. Applying flat-term K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] makes this a derived equality: the bidegree comparisons are natural in each differential and hence commute with their sum $d_M\otimes1+(-1)^{\deg M}1\otimes d_N$; the total maps agree on each summand. Pullback of the tensor is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Thus the displayed identity holds for the actual derived interchange, not only on cohomology. For two successive opens the corresponding tensor/composition identity is the same sectionwise identity, totalized in the same way.

To apply these calculations, use the standard compatible projective compactifications of the coordinate tower: compactify the first $d$ coordinates by $(\mathbf P^1_Y)^d$ and the last by the relative projective line. Equivalently use the compatible compactifications supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]. All their schemes are finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian. They are quasi-compact by the Noetherian convention and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; every open here is quasi-compact. The normalization in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] expresses the ordinary compact-support compositor as proper/open interchange followed by the proper and open compositors; it restricts to [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] on our bounded-below inputs. The finite evaluation assertion in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] identifies that interchange with its pro-etale realization. Together with [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], these are the comparisons defining [thm-sf-comp-composition] on the witnessed objects. Expanding the compactification formula [def-exchange-projection], the proper-composition identity of the first paragraph, the displayed proper/open tensor identity, and the open-composition identity therefore give
$$\operatorname{PF}_{gf,M,N}\circ(\alpha_{g,f,M}\otimes1)
=\alpha_{g,f,M\otimes P_fP_gN}\circ Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,P_gN})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{g,Rf_!M,N}.$$
This is the required compatibility with the specified compact-support compositor for the coordinate projections $f,g$; the formula uses the canonical pullback compositors. It has been proved from the defining maps at this finite coefficient level. In its applications below $M=L_q$ or a tensor of shifted Tate lines. The direct image $Rq_!L_q\cong A_{X_d}$ is bounded constructible by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] and the site comparison of Step 1. The base factors are $K$, its pullbacks, or a Tate line tensored with such a pullback, so they are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and local freeness of the Tate lines. Choose etale witnesses using [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and transfer their Tor intervals by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii). Every projection map to be inverted in this identity is thus invertible by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], on exactly its stated witnessed domain. We only need the identity for these chosen compatible compactifications; no general all-coefficient coherence theorem is used.

Finally $P_{p,K}$ is the ordered affine-line comparison. In rank one, the displayed definition of $\Gamma_{p,K}$ (agreeing with [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] on its domain) is the transpose of the projective-line trace restricted to the affine line, with the projection formula. This is exactly the affine-line integration used in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. More precisely, [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] states that the actual projective-line counit at every $K$ is $(1_K\otimes t_q)\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$. Composing with the open-extension adjunction specified in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] restricts $t_q$ to $I_S$; projection-map composition compatibility therefore gives the same formula for the actual affine-line counit, not just for its value at the tensor unit. Suppose the identification has been checked for $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$, and write $q:\mathbf A^{d+1}_Y\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ for the last-coordinate projection. Use the explicit affine adjunctions $F_d\dashv G_d$ and $F_1\dashv G_1$ of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], whose right adjoints are twisted pullbacks. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], their composite counit at $K$ is $\varepsilon_{p_d,K}\circ Rp_{d!}(\varepsilon_{q,G_dK})$, where $G_dK=p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ and the two $\varepsilon$ here denote the counits of these explicit affine adjunctions. Their identification with the actual exceptional adjunctions is through the integration transposes $P$, not an identification of their right adjoints by notation alone. By definition the trace $t_{p_{d+1}}$ in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] is the counit of precisely this composite, and [def-amb-vector-integration] uses that trace on a trivial bundle. Write $L_d=A_{X_d}(d)[2d]$ and $L_q=A_{X_{d+1}}(1)[2]$. Under the coherent pullback/tensor and compact-support composition identifications of Step 1, the composition compatibility just proved rewrites that composite counit as
$$
K\otimes Rp_{d!}(L_d\otimes Rq_!L_q)
\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes Rp_{d!}(1_{L_d}\otimes t_q)}
K\otimes Rp_{d!}L_d
\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes t_{p_d}}K.
$$
Here $t_q$ is the affine-line counit at the tensor unit. At $K=A_Y$ the same displayed composite is $t_{p_{d+1}}$, by its definition as the composite counit. Thus at general $K$ the displayed map is $1_K\otimes t_{p_{d+1}}$ after the projection isomorphism. The composition identification for the pro-etale compact-support functors is [thm-sf-comp-composition]; the current definition [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] specifies its conjugate $c_d$ on exceptional inverse images. Its recursion applies the last affine-line map to $Rp_d^!K$, whereas the explicit composite adjunction first uses $G_dK=Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]$. Both inputs have the required bounded constructible finite-Tor domain: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] applies to the separated finite-type projection $p_d$ and gives $Lp_d^*K$ bounded constructible with the same Tor interval as $K$. Tensor with the locally free Tate line is exact and preserves finite local constancy on each constructible stratum, and the shift translates the finite cohomological and Tor intervals, so $G_dK$ has these properties; Step 5 identifies $Rp_d^!K$ with $G_dK$. These agree: naturality of the affine-line transpose (from naturality of its defining projection map) gives
$$\Gamma_{q,Rp_d^!K}\circ Lq^*(P_{p_d,K})(1)[2]
=Rq^!(P_{p_d,K})\circ\Gamma_{q,G_dK}.$$
Substituting this equation and the induction hypothesis into the recursion of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], its transpose is exactly the composite counit just computed. Taking that transpose gives the ordered composite of the already identified $d$ affine-line comparisons and the last affine-line comparison, with the exceptional-composition and twist-additivity isomorphisms. This is the ordered recursion defining $\Gamma$ in the statement, and [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] on its original domain. The induction starts with the identity adjunction at $d=0$. All shifts added are even, so these reassociations introduce no sign. The specific comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies the projection/integration maps and their transposes, and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] supplies the corresponding hom bijections. Applying comparison pullback to the computed equality and inserting those identifications gives this equality in the stated pro-etale category. Together with Step 5 it proves the claimed agreement for every $K$, including $K=0$.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
for the projection $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ the smooth purity map
$\gamma_{p_d,K}$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] equals the
affinity-space purity comparison of [cor-pur-affine-space-purity],
i.e. the ordered composite of the $d$ affinity-line purity maps of
[thm-pur-affine-line-purity].

proof.text:
Both maps are canonical and, by [thm-pur-composition-coherence]
and [prop-pur-affine-space-purity-compatibilities], they are
compatible with the tower of affine projections. It therefore suffices
to compare them after restriction to a geometric fiber of $Y$, where
both are determined by the Kummer computation: the dualizing-object
identification of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] for $p_d$ comes
from the deformation of the diagonal $\Delta$ and the standard-pair
computation of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4) – the diagonal
of the standard pair $(\mathbf A^{2d}_Y,\Delta)$ has normal bundle the
trivial rank-$d$ bundle $T_{p_d}$, and the DNC invariance of
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] is the identity on the standard pair –
whose class, by
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry] and the definition of the
[def-pur-frame-class] (class of a frame), is the $d$-fold
exterior product of the rank-one Kummer boundaries, i.e. the
$d$-fold product of the affinity-line orientations; the affinity-space
purity of [cor-pur-affine-space-purity] is built from exactly the
same $d$-fold product of the affinity-line orientations. The two
assemblies differ only by the canonical reassociations of the package
(the Koszul signs are $+1$, since all shift factors are of even
degree, by [prop-pur-affine-space-purity-compatibilities]); hence
the maps agree.
